**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/07/20 (Thu) 18:12
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Logical matrices, also known as logical matrices of Ryszard Wójcicki, are a mathematical model used in non-classical logics to describe the truth values of propositions in different states of a system.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Defined terms: M (the man), B (the bartender), ID (the man's identification), T (the man's age), S (the set of possible states of the system), walk(bar) (the action of walking into a bar), ask(beer) (the action of asking for a beer), ask(ID, M) (the action of asking M for ID), claim(not(have(ID))) (the action of claiming not to have ID), ask(T, M) (the action of asking M how old he is), reply(T=21) (the action of replying that T is equal to 21), ask(T=21, not(have(ID)), M) (the action of asking M how he can be 21 years old if he does not have any ID), respond(time_traveler(future)) (the action of responding that he is a time traveler from the future), exist(ID, time_period(M)) (the existence of ID in the time period of M).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided a logical matrix example with two states and various propositions, including truth values for each proposition in those states.
- [USER] Expressed uncertainty about the type of logical matrices being discussed and requested a revision to include a set of truth-values, a subset of designated truth-values, and an interpretation function for logical connectives.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Acknowledged the difference in logical matrices and provided a revised formal semantics using logical matrices, including the same defined terms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Defined a set of truth-values as {0, 1} where 0 represents "false" and 1 represents "true", and designated truth-values as {1}.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided an interpretation function for logical connectives: ¬, ∧, ∨, and → with specific outputs based on inputs.
- [USER] Requested to internalize the strings "M" and "walk" as logical connectives and suggested using more than three truth-values.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Agreed to revise the formal semantics using logical matrices with three truth-values and defined the truth-values as {-1, 0, 1} where -1 represents "neither true nor false", 0 represents "false", and 1 represents "true".
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Defined designated truth-values as {1, -1}.
